Title: Former MAG chief Izham Ismail appointed to Maybank board
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has appointed former Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) group managing director and airline group chief executive officer Datuk Captain Izham Ismail as an independent non-executive director effective Nov 15.
Maybank announced the appointment in a Bursa Malaysia filing today.
Izham, 65, led MAG as group managing director and airline group CEO from 2017 until 2026, retiring from the airline group on Jan 31 this year.
A veteran of Malaysia's aviation industry, he joined Malaysia Airlines as a pilot in 1979 before moving into a series of senior operational and management roles.
Among his previous positions were chief revenue officer from 2019 to 2023, group chief operations officer between 2016 and 2017, and chief executive officer of MASwings Sdn Bhd in 2016.
His appointment brings extensive aviation, operational and corporate leadership experience to the board of Malaysia's largest banking group.
According to the filing, Izham does not hold any other directorships in public companies or listed issuers and has no interest in Maybank securities.
The appointment comes as Maybank navigates a softer earnings performance in the first half of its 2026 financial year.
For the six months ended June 30, 2026, Maybank's net profit edged down to RM5.17 billion from RM5.22 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier.
Revenue fell 8.7 per cent to RM30.99 billion, compared with RM33.95 billion previously

Title: Selangor allocates RM559mil to replace ageing water pipes
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Selangor has allocated RM559 million in its 2027 Budget to replace ageing water pipes as part of efforts to improve the state's water supply system.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said more than 6,000km of ageing pipes needed to be replaced, with 1,231.01km already replaced as of August 2026.
The annual replacement target was increased from 150km to 300km in 2024 to speed up the programme, which began in 2016.
Another RM143.2 million has been allocated to upgrade water treatment plants, while RM209.2 million will go towards the Water Grid Connectivity project.
The project aims to achieve 100 per cent connectivity for 36 dam terminals by the end of 2028, strengthening the water supply systems in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.
Separately, the state government will provide a RM250 million loan to Worldwide Holdings Berhad to build its third Waste-to-Energy plant in Tanjung Dua Belas, which will include a recycling materials recovery facility.
The second Waste-to-Energy plant is scheduled to begin operations in the first quarter of 2027. It will have the capacity to process 3,000 tonnes of waste a day and generate 52 megawatts of electricity.

Title: Selangor to give 5,000 p-hailing riders RM100 monthly voucher
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Some 5,000 registered p-hailing riders in Selangor will receive RM100 monthly, or RM1,200 annually, under the Kita Selangor Gig Voucher initiative announced in the Selangor 2027 Budget.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the initiative recognised the riders' contribution to the logistics sector and the income risks they faced due to illness or accidents.
He said many gig workers continued to struggle to secure permanent employment, partly because their skills did not match industry requirements.
"To address this challenge, the state government will provide the Kita Selangor Gig Voucher of RM100 a month, equivalent to RM1,200 a year, to 5,000 registered p-hailing riders to ease their financial burden," he said when tabling the RM3.3 billion Selangor 2027 Budget at the state legislative assembly sitting here today.
Amirudin said the voucher would be complemented by technology exposure and industry training through short courses conducted by the Selangor Technical Skills Development Centre (STDC).
The programme, including training, would receive an allocation of RM10 million, he said.
Meanwhile, the state government has allocated RM12 million to help residents harness productivity gains from artificial intelligence (AI).
In collaboration with STDC and Google, the state will provide 50,000 Selangorians with one-year access to Gemini Enterprise, alongside online and in-person training.
Amirudin said the programme would equip participants from various backgrounds, including students, entrepreneurs, farmers, start-up founders and senior citizens, with skills to develop agentic AI systems to improve productivity and simplify daily tasks.

Title: Seventh victim found after water surge at Sungai Pertak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The body of an Indian citizen was found during a search and rescue operation following a water surge at Sungai Luit, Kampung Orang Asli Pertak, Kuala Kubu Baru.
The discovery brings the number of victims found to seven out of eight, with one man still missing.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department director Datuk Wan Md Razali Wan Ismail said the seventh body was found at 3.40pm in Sector C of the search area.
He said the body was taken to Sungai Buloh Hospital.
The search and rescue operation is continuing to find the remaining missing victim.
Eight men, including one Malaysian and seven foreigners, were swept away by strong currents during a water surge at Sungai Luit last Monday.
Five victims were found on Tuesday, while the
sixth body was recovered near the Sungai Selangor Dam
yesterday.

Title: WCT Holdings appoints Lai Cheng Yee as group MD
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: WCT Holdings Bhd has appointed Lai Cheng Yee as its group managing director (MD) beginning today.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, WCT said Lai, 52, has over 20 years of professional experience working in local conglomerates such as BIG Industries Bhd, the Pavilion Group, Diethelm Malaysia, Procter & Gamble and F&N Malaysia.
"Lai joined WCT Holdings as director (executive chairman's office) on Aug 15, 2018, assisting the executive chairman across all the group's businesses.
"She has headed the group's hospitality, aviation and food and beverage (F&B) divisions since June 1, 2024, and has undertaken the group's concession-related projects and oversees the engineering and construction and property development divisions," it said.
Lai holds 13,527 shares in WCT Holdings.
She is also an associate member of the Chartered Governance Institute of Malaysia.
Meanwhile, Lai has served as a board member of Tourism Malaysia since Sept 8, 2023, where she collaborates with other industry leaders to support the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture of Malaysia (MOTAC) in promoting the growth of the Malaysian tourism industry.
She also serves as a non-independent non-executive director of Paradigm Reit Management Sdn Bhd, the manager of Paradigm Real Estate Investment Trust (Reit).

Title: Altantuya family's bid to appeal damages set for Feb 25
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court has fixed Feb 25 next year to hear an application by Altantuya Shaariibuu's family for leave to appeal against a ruling reducing damages over her murder.
Lawyer Abraham Au, representing political analyst Abdul Razak Baginda, said the date was set following case management before Federal Court deputy registrar Rohaiza Hamzah yesterday.
He said the court also fixed Dec 3 to hear the family's application to amend its notice of motion seeking leave to appeal.
Altantuya's family filed the leave application on Feb 19 this year after the Court of Appeal reduced the damages awarded to them from RM5 million to RM1.4 million.
On Jan 20, the appellate court also ruled that the government was not vicariously liable for the actions of former police officers Sirul Azhar Umar and Azilah Hadri.
The family of the murdered Mongolian citizen had filed a RM100 million civil suit against Abdul Razak, Azilah, Sirul Azhar and the government in 2007, claiming her death caused them mental shock and psychological trauma.
In 2022, the Shah Alam High Court ordered the defendants to pay RM5 million in damages to the family.
Azilah and Sirul Azhar were convicted of Altantuya's murder in 2009. The Court of Appeal later acquitted them, before the Federal Court overturned the acquittals and reinstated their convictions in 2015.
In 2023, the Federal Court commuted Azilah's death sentence to 40 years' imprisonment after allowing his review application under the Revision of Sentence of Death and Imprisonment for Natural Life (Temporary Jurisdiction of the Federal Court) Act 2023.

Title: Sabah east coast security boosts tourism confidence
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah's east coast has recorded no kidnapping cases since Jan 15, 2020, boosting foreign tourists' confidence in the area's security.
Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Victor Sanjos said the achievement was the result of continued efforts by previous leaders and close cooperation among various agencies to maintain security.
"We have maintained a record of zero kidnappings since Jan 15, 2020, continuing the efforts of previous leaders.
"Improved security has allowed development along Sabah's east coast to progress and created more economic opportunities for local communities.
"It has also prompted most foreign countries to lower their travel advisories for the area from levels two and three to level one," he said after paying a courtesy call on Sabah Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Musa Aman at Istana Seri Kinabalu.
Victor said the lower travel advisory levels had also contributed to an increase in foreign tourist arrivals in Sabah.
Sabah's east coast is home to some of the region's best-known diving destinations, including Sipadan Island, which attracts divers from around the world for its rich marine life and coral reefs.
He said the visit was to formally inform Musa of his appointment as Sabah Police Commissioner and introduce Eastern Sabah Security Command (ESSCOM) commander Datuk Abdul Fuad Abdul Malek, who took over the post on Nov 11.
Victor said he was confident Fuad's extensive experience and knowledge of security matters in Sabah would help maintain security in the ESSCOM area.

Title: DXN eyes Venezuela opportunities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: DXN Holdings Bhd has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Venezuela's La Guaira Special Economic Zone (La Guaira SEZ) to explore potential investment and business opportunities in sustainable agriculture, aquaculture, agro-processing and manufacturing.
The MoU signed on Nov 9 also covers cooperation to support the development of a halal ecosystem in Venezuela.
DXN group chief executive officer Prajith Pavithran said working with La Guaira SEZ gives the company a way to assess new sources of raw materials and explore how local processing could support its Latin American operations.
"We also see an opportunity to share our experience in Malaysia's halal industry with the relevant Venezuelan authorities," he said in a statement.
The MoU was signed in Caracas by La Guaira SEZ sole auhority Marcos Meléndez and DXN project director Foo Wai Leong.
Meléndez said the cooperation aims to encourage joint research and attract investment in the sectors covered by the MoU in the state of La Guaira.
The Venezuelan government established La Guaira SEZ in 2023 to attract domestic and foreign investment to La Guaira.
Its priority sectors include industrial development, technology, logistics and transport, tourism and agro-food.
Under the five-year MoU, La Guaira SEZ may facilitate the identification of suitable land for potential plantation development.
The parties may also explore biofertilisers, technology transfer and training, as well as ways to support Venezuelan authorities in developing halal certification infrastructure.

Title: Melaka polls: Ab Rauf leads 3,000-strong motorcycle convoy in Tanjung Bidara
Article:
MASJID TANAH: More than 3,000 motorcycles took part in a Barisan Nasional convoy across the Tanjung Bidara state constituency on the final day of campaigning for the Melaka election today.
The convoy, held as part of a flash mob programme, was led by Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh, who is also the coalition's candidate for the Tanjung Bidara seat.
Starting from the Kampung Pulau Polling District Centre (PDM) about 4pm, the convoy travelled to six PDMs across the constituency, including Lubok Redan, Pengkalan Balak and Pasir Gembur, before concluding about 5.30pm.
At each location, members of the public welcomed the convoy by waving BN flags and holding banners in support of Ab Rauf.
The same programme was also held across Melaka, with the participation of 7,000 motorcycles, it is understood.
Ab Rauf said youth groups and Wanita Umno had organised the programme as BN's final campaign push to encourage voters to turn out on polling day tomorrow.
"More than 3,000 motorcycles joined me today.
"The reception along our journey through the contested state constituencies was very encouraging, particularly among young people," he said.
Ab Rauf also urged voters to fulfil their responsibility by casting their ballots tomorrow.
"Do not forget to come out and vote tomorrow. Let us go together to fulfil our responsibility as Malaysians. Red pen, blue pen, vote blue, I love you," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit ends mostly higher against major currencies, eases versus greenback
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended mostly higher against major currencies but eased against the US dollar on Friday as the greenback continued its upward momentum on a hawkish US interest rate outlook.
The market has been expecting a sizeable interest rate hike by the US Federal Reserve (Fed) when the American central bank meets in December.
At 6pm, the local currency depreciated to 4.0845/0890 against the greenback from 4.0765/0805 at Thursday's close.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar continued to be lifted as investors anticipated further monetary tightening by the Fed at its upcoming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting next month.  "Based on interest rate futures contracts, a 25 basis-point rate hike is widely anticipated, with the probability of an increase currently indicated at 111 per cent," he told Bernama.
Attention is now shifting towards whether the Fed will opt for a more aggressive 50-basis-point hike in a single move, potentially providing further support for the greenback, he added.
The ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies.
It strengthened against the euro to 4.5166/5216 from 4.5225/5269 at Thursday's close, appreciated vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.4046/4106 from 5.4103/4156, but edged down against the Japanese yen to 2.5549/5579 from 2.5524/5551.
However, the ringgit traded mostly lower against its Asean peers.
It inched down against the Singapore dollar to 3.1729/1769 from 3.1726/1760, fell vis-à-vis the Indonesian rupiah to 224.3/224.6 from 223.5/223.8 and declined against the Philippine peso to 6.41/6.42 from 6.40/6.41.
It climbed against the Thai baht to 12.0611/0833 from 12.0678/0836.

Title: Selangor announces two-month special financial aid for civil servants
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor government today announced a Special Financial Assistance (BKK) payment equivalent to two months' salary for state civil servants.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the incentive is a token of appreciation for civil servants' hard work in delivering aid to the people, particularly through the Pakej Pengukuhan Daya Tahan Selangor.
He said the package has helped empower vulnerable groups, school students, working women, farmers and padi farmers as they navigate the global energy crisis.
"The state government is announcing the 'Kita Selangor' Special Financial Assistance (BKK) for the year 2026, amounting to two months' salary or allowance, with a minimum payment of RM1,000.
"This payment will be drawn from current-year allocations and will cover the emoluments of state government personnel, including those whose salaries are paid by the federal government as well as teachers of 'Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain' religious classes, with a total financial implication of RM100.31 million.
"God willing, the 'Kita Selangor' BKK will be disbursed by Dec 21," he said while tabling the Selangor 2027 Budget today.

Title: AAPA adopts four aviation resolutions, urges government support amid rising fuel costs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Association of Asia Pacific Airlines (AAPA) has adopted four resolutions covering aviation sustainability, passenger rights, cabin safety and aviation security, while calling on governments to support airlines facing sharply higher fuel prices and operating costs.
The resolutions were adopted at the close of AAPA's 70th Assembly of Presidents, hosted by Malaysia Airlines Bhd here today.
AAPA director general Wong Hong said Asia Pacific airlines are operating in a more challenging environment compared with 12 months ago.
"The operating environment for Asia Pacific airlines has changed markedly since the last Assembly of Presidents 12 months ago. Carriers have continued to demonstrate resilience and adaptability."
"However, the sharp escalation in fuel prices, coupled with other cost pressures and operational uncertainties, has created a far more demanding environment," he said at a press conference today.
Wong urged governments to work closely with the aviation industry to address the growing financial and operational pressures facing airlines.
"Governments must recognise these pressures and work constructively with the industry to provide support that safeguards the long-term viability of air transport across the region," he said.
AAPA also called for closer cooperation among governments, aviation regulators and industry stakeholders to address common challenges and strengthen the long-term competitiveness of Asia Pacific aviation.
Under the first resolution on aviation sustainability, the association reaffirmed its target of achieving five per cent sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) utilisation by 2030.
This is in support of the International Civil Aviation Organisation's (ICAO) long-term goal of achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2050.
AAPA has asked governments to adopt eight key policy principles when developing national and regional SAF policies.
The principles include providing long-term policy clarity, encouraging competition among SAF producers and suppliers, preventing market concentration and ensuring fair treatment for airlines.
The association also called for policies that support different SAF production technologies based on their ability to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, rather than favouring a particular technology.
It wants governments to establish clear SAF certification requirements, preferably based on ICAO's Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA).
AAPA also asked governments to align national and international SAF policies while allowing airlines greater flexibility in purchasing SAF, including through the book-and-claim system.
On passenger rights, AAPA called on governments to balance consumer protection with airline competitiveness when introducing or reviewing regulations.
It said passenger protection rules should ensure travellers receive clear information before their flights, regular updates and appropriate assistance during disruptions, as well as efficient complaint-handling procedures.
However, AAPA stressed that responsibility for flight disruptions should be shared fairly among aviation stakeholders, rather than placing a disproportionate burden on airlines.
The association also called for closer cooperation among aviation stakeholders in planning for and managing disruptions, while ensuring passengers have fair and non-discriminatory access to air transport.
The third resolution focuses on strengthening cabin safety through greater cooperation among governments, regulators and airlines.
AAPA identified several areas requiring closer attention, including risks involving lithium batteries, unruly passengers, medical emergencies, aircraft evacuations and cabin crew training.
It also called on aviation regulators across the region to strengthen information sharing and cooperation in developing their regulatory capabilities.
Under the fourth resolution on aviation security, the association called for greater regional collaboration to address human factors that could affect security operations.
These include personnel training, workload management, security culture and organisational learning.
AAPA also encouraged aviation authorities to share best practices through ICAO's Asia and Pacific aviation security forum.
Wong said the four resolutions outlined the industry's priorities in strengthening aviation sustainability, safety, security and resilience.
"These resolutions show how Asia Pacific airlines intend to build an aviation industry that is sustainable, safe, secure and resilient."
"AAPA and its members stand ready to work with governments, regulators and partners across the industry to deliver it, so that Asia Pacific aviation continues to drive growth and connectivity across the region and beyond," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lawyer: Former model's family will not appeal RM1.1mil damages ruling
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The family of Dutch model Ivana Smit will not appeal a ruling overturning a RM1.1 million damages award over alleged police negligence in the investigation into her death.
The family's lawyer, Datuk Sankara Nair, said it would not seek leave to appeal to the Federal Court against the Court of Appeal's decision in October, bringing the civil proceedings to an end.
However, he said the decision should not be interpreted as the family being satisfied with the police investigation or believing that its concerns had been addressed.
"Their decision deserves respect and should not be understood as satisfaction with the investigation or acceptance that their concerns have been answered," he said in a statement.
In October, the Court of Appeal set aside a High Court ruling ordering the government to pay RM1.1 million in damages to the mother of Dutch model Ivana Smit over alleged negligence in the investigation into her daughter's death.
https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/10/1554997/updated-court-appeal-overturns-rm11mil-award-ivana-smits-mother-watch
The appellate court also ruled that findings from earlier inquest and criminal revision proceedings could not, on their own, establish civil liability in a separate trial.
Sankara said the ruling raised concerns about the legal remedies available to families who believed investigations into the deaths of their loved ones had been mishandled.
"The implication is troubling for bereaved families: a legal obligation to investigate a death does not necessarily provide those most directly affected with a remedy in damages when that investigation is alleged to have failed."
He said that while the ruling did not grant blanket immunity to public authorities, it created a substantial obstacle for families seeking damages over alleged investigative negligence.
He also called for stronger independent oversight and legislative consideration to ensure accountability when civil remedies were restricted.
Sankara welcomed the Court of Appeal's stern oral remarks when delivering its decision, particularly its reminder that the ruling did not absolve the police of past shortcomings.
He said the court had emphasised the police's continuing responsibility to pursue viable leads diligently and keep Smit's family regularly informed of developments.
However, these observations were made orally and did not form part of a formal court order requiring the authorities to provide updates.
"The conclusion of this civil action leaves the authorities' investigative responsibilities intact.
"We call upon them to heed the Court's oral observations through sustained investigative effort and clear, regular communication with Ivana's family.
"The family has chosen to bring its civil litigation to a close. The authorities must continue their work towards establishing the truth surrounding Ivana's death."
Smit, 18, was found dead on the balcony of a sixth-floor unit at CapSquare Residence here on Dec 7, 2017, after she was believed to have fallen from a condominium unit on the 20th floor.
Police initially classified the case as sudden death before a coroner ruled in March 2019 that her death was due to misadventure.
In November 2019, the High Court overturned the coroner's findings and ruled that her death was caused by persons known or unknown.

Title: Policeman injured in parang attack can now move fingers after surgery
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A policeman who was severely injured in a parang attack in Kepong is showing positive recovery and is now able to move several fingers on his injured hand.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad had informed the cabinet of the update during its meeting today.
"The police officer has shown positive progress and can move several fingers of the affected hand," he said at his weekly post-cabinet press conference today.
Fahmi said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had explained that existing procedures allowed policemen to take necessary action to protect themselves during operations, with personal safety remaining the priority.
He said the Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had also expressed concern over the attack.
Lance Corporal Thierry Rodger Fendy, 26, who is attached to the Gombak police headquarters, sustained injuries to his
right hand
during a confrontation with an armed foreigner at an apartment in Desa Amanpuri on Wednesday.
Yesterday, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the complex
replantation surgery
took eight hours and was performed by HKL's Upper Limb and Microsurgery subspecialty team, led by Dr Allan Ravi Rajagopal and Dr Aziz Sabbir Husain.
Earlier, Anwar congratulated the HKL surgical team for successfully
reattaching
the officer's severed hand.

Title: Najib performs Friday prayers in Kajang Prison
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak performed Friday prayers in Kajang Prison today, the Prisons Department confirmed.
This was Najib's first Friday prayers since being allowed to spend the remainder of his SRC International jail sentence under house arrest at his residence in Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta.
Earlier, media reports said Najibwas seen leaving his residence about 10.30am in a Proton X70 which was escorted by Prisons Department and police vehicles.
Yesterday, his son, Datuk Mohd Nazifuddin, had said Najib would perform Friday prayers in Kajang Prison, in line with stipulations from the Prisons Department.
On Tuesday, the Kuala Lumpur High Court issued an order for Najib to spend his remaining sentence for the SRC International case — until Aug 23, 2028 — under
house arrest
.
This was after his fine of RM50 million was settled.

Title: Kedah MB's daughter injured in motorcycle crash
Article:
ALOR STAR: Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor's daughter was seriously injured when her motorcycle crashed near Kampung Alor Setol.
She suffered injuries to her face and head, as well as fractures to four fingers and her ribs, in the accident yesterday.
She is being treated in the intensive care unit (ICU) of Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital.
Sanusi said his third child remained in the ICU for close monitoring and further tests to check for possible internal injuries.
"Doctors have advised that she remain under close observation. She may be moved to a general ward tomorrow if her condition improves following further examinations," he said here today.
He said his daughter, a tahfiz student, was enrolled in a fast-track programme at Kolej Islam Darul Ulum in Pokok Sena to prepare for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination.
Her injuries, particularly to her right hand, are expected to prevent her from sitting the examination, which begins on Nov 23.
Meanwhile, Kota Setar district police chief Assistant Commissioner Syed Basri Syed Ali said preliminary investigations found that the accident occurred about 4pm when the 20-year-old was riding a Yamaha X-Max 250 from her college in Pokok Sena towards Alor Star.
"She is believed to have lost control of the motorcycle upon reaching the location, causing it to veer off the road and into a drain," he said in a statement last night.

Title: 1,764 flood victims remain at 12 relief centres in three states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,764 flood victims from 475 families remain housed at 12 temporary relief centres across three states as at 4.30pm today.
According to the Social Welfare Department's Info Bencana portal, the affected states are Selangor, Perak and Sarawak.
Selangor recorded the highest number, with 1,454 victims from 390 families taking shelter at eight relief centres in the Kuala Selangor district.
In Perak, 274 victims from 79 families are housed at two relief centres in the Hilir Perak district.
In Sarawak, 35 victims from six families remain at two relief centres across the Kuching and Miri districts.
Of the total victims, 1,137 are adult men and women, including 122 senior citizens, while 634 are children and 53 are infants.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm, heavy rain and strong wind warning for six states and a federal territory until 7pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covers Terengganu (Hulu Terengganu, Dungun and Setiu), Pahang (Jerantut, Rompin and Cameron Highlands) and Johor (Segamat, Batu Pahat, Kluang, Muar, Tangkak, Kulai, Johor Bahru, Pontian and Kota Tinggi).
Similar weather conditions are forecast in Sarawak, affecting Marudi, Miri, Limbang, Bintulu, Mukah and Sibu.
In Sabah, the warning involves the Interior divisions of Sipitang, Tenom and Pensiangan, Tawau, Kudat, the West Coast divisions of Kota Belud, Tuaran and Kota Kinabalu, as well as the entire Federal Territory of Labuan.

Title: Two Bangladeshis nabbed as Penang Immigration officers bust fake e-pass syndicate
Article:
SEBERANG JAYA: The Penang Immigration Department crippled a fake immigration e-pass printing syndicate and arrested two Bangladeshi men in Simpang Ampat last night.
State Immigration director Syamsul Fitry Ahmad said the suspects, aged 23 and 32, were detained during a 10pm raid at a rented house following public tip-offs and days of intelligence gathering.
"During the inspection of the premises, we discovered several forged or altered e-pass printouts, including documents bearing the particulars of one of the suspects as well as other foreigners.
"The team also found several foreign passports not belonging to the suspects, alongside a large quantity of altered e-pass printouts believed ready for distribution to buyers," he told reporters at the Penang Immigration headquarters.
Syamsul Fitry said further checks revealed the forged documents were linked to the construction sector, with the syndicate targeting undocumented or overstaying Bangladeshi and Pakistani nationals.
He said the syndicate's modus operandi involved digitally editing details on e-pass and passport copies using a laptop before printing them to deceive authorities and employers.
He said the syndicate was believed to have only started operating recently, adding that it charged between RM50 and RM100 per fake e-pass.
However, he said payment transaction records suggest higher fees may have been collected from some, given that genuine annual renewals start at RM2,000.
"So far, we have detected over 50 suspected forged documents, though the exact number remains under investigation based on evidence recovered at the scene and inside the suspects' laptops and mobile phones," he said.
Enforcement officers also seized mobile phones, laptops and printers used to produce the documents, alongside a car and two motorcycles suspected of being used in the syndicate's operations.
Syamsul Fitry added that while the 23-year-old suspect held a valid passport and construction sector work pass, his accomplice was undocumented.
Investigations are ongoing to determine if the duo are linked to a wider network, he added.
"Physically, the fake e-passes are difficult to detect as they look nearly identical to genuine ones, but immigration officers can verify them through QR code scans and counter system checks," he said.
Both suspects have been remanded for 14 days.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka election: Parties told to stop campaigning by midnight
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Political parties, candidates and their supporters must stop all campaigning, including on social media, by 11.59pm tonight ahead of Saturday's Melaka election.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said parties should not publish new campaign-related content after the deadline set by the Election Commission (EC).
He said candidates and parties should issue their final campaign messages early to avoid breaching election rules.
Fahmi also said voters should cast their ballots early, as rain was expected in several areas.
"For those returning to their hometowns to fulfil their responsibility as voters in Melaka, drive safely, ensure you have enough rest, that your vehicles are well-maintained, and do not drive above the speed limit," he said.
He said the police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission would continue monitoring possible offences, including those committed on social media.
Fahmi said the public should rely on verified information from official sources, including the EC's social media platforms and established news organisations, and avoid sharing unverified content from parties with vested interests.
"Please verify, because we find it is not impossible that certain parties may produce content of questionable authenticity. Refer to official sources," he said.
The EC is targeting a voter turnout of
70 per cent in Saturday's
election.
The 16th Melaka election will
see 79 candidates
contesting 28 seats.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Prisons Department aims to expand family rehab programme nationwide to curb recidivism
Article:
NIBONG TEBAL: The Prisons Department plans to expand a new family and parenting rehabilitation module nationwide to reduce recidivism rates among inmates.
Prisons Deputy Commissioner-General (Security and Correctional) Rosoman Abu Bakar @ Che Din said the pioneer initiative, Kompas Sejahtera, equipped inmates with essential life skills prior to their reintegration into society.
He said the pilot run involved 30 facilitators from the northern zone correctional institutions — covering Penang, Kedah, Perlis and Perak — and directly benefited 224 male inmates at the Seberang Prai Prison.
"We hope the module owner will allow the Prisons Department to roll out these modules across all correctional institutions in Malaysia," he said at the programme's closing ceremony.
The event was officiated by state Social Development, Welfare and Non-Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Lim Siew Khim.
Kompas Sejahtera was developed through strategic collaborations with Universiti Utara Malaysia and the National Population and Family Development Board.
Rosoman said the department is also working to certify the facilitators' training and is considering submitting the initiative for recognition in the Malaysia Book of Records.
"Inmates who are about to be released must possess the awareness, knowledge and skills to return as responsible fathers, husbands and members of society. This directly reduces the risk of re-offending," he said.
He added that the training modules should also be extended to prison personnel to strengthen their roles as leaders and agents of change within the correctional system.
Addressing the inmates, Rosoman urged them to treat the programme as a turning point, reminding them that a father's responsibility goes beyond material provision to include love, attention, education, guidance and character building.
"Your past is not an obstacle to building a more meaningful future. Opportunities to change are always there, every second, provided you take that first step," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bursa courts regional retail investors via new partnership
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia Bhd is seeking to widen foreign retail participation in the local stock market through a partnership with Singapore brokerage Phillip Nova, as it looks to attract more regional investors to Malaysian-listed companies.
The collaboration, launched in Singapore on Nov 7 under Bursa Malaysia's Invest Beyond Borders initiative, is intended to give Singapore-based retail investors easier access to Malaysian equities through Phillip Nova's digital trading platform.
The inaugural investor engagement attracted more than 800 registrations, with six Malaysian-listed companies presenting their businesses and growth prospects to potential investors.
The companies were Top Glove Corp Bhd, Karex Bhd, Inta Bina Group Bhd, Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd, Hi-Mobility Bhd and Kee Ming Group Bhd.
Investors were given briefings by company representatives on their business fundamentals, strategies and outlook, alongside access to market information and corporate insights.
Bursa Malaysia director of group commercial and market coverage Stephanie Tan said the partnership was part of efforts to make local equities more visible to investors across the region.
She said the response to the inaugural event indicated interest among Singapore investors in exploring Malaysian companies.
The exchange will seek to expand similar partnerships with overseas brokers and digital investment platforms.
Phillip Nova chief executive officer Teyu Che Chern said Malaysian equities could offer Singapore investors another avenue for portfolio diversification and exposure to regional growth.
The collaboration comes as Bursa Malaysia seeks to address the need for stronger research coverage, investor engagement and visibility of listed companies beyond the domestic market.
Other initiatives include the Research Incentive Scheme Plus (RISE+), which supports research coverage of listed companies, and IR4U, which helps companies improve investor relations and engagement with shareholders.
The exchange is also promoting its Bursa Malaysia Quality 50 and BMQ Shariah indices, which recorded year-to-date returns of about nine per cent and 12 per cent respectively as at October 2026.
These efforts complement its MY Value Up programme, aimed at encouraging listed companies to improve corporate performance and long-term value creation.
Bursa Malaysia said it will continue working with international brokerage partners to expand access to local equities and connect Malaysian companies with a wider pool of regional investors.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia-Indonesia ties remain strong despite Gibran's resignation, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia-Indonesia ties will remain unaffected by the resignation of Indonesian vice-president Gibran Rakabuming Raka, said government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the political developments in Indonesia would not affect the longstanding ties between the neighbouring countries.
"Relations between the two countries will remain intact and remain good. I just returned from Jakarta a few weeks ago.
"Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi also made an official visit to Indonesia and held a meeting with the president recently.
"We believe that the good relations between both countries will continue to remain strong and intact, regardless of what happens," he told reporters at his weekly post-cabinet press conference here today.
Gibran, 39, the son of former Indonesian president Joko Widodo,
announced his resignation
on Wednesday amid mounting scrutiny over his eligibility following court rulings concerning his educational qualifications.
He formally submitted his resignation to Indonesia's People's Consultative Assembly yesterday.
The resignation came amid growing political tensions surrounding President Prabowo Subianto's alliance with Widodo, who backed Prabowo's presidential bid in 2024 after previously defeating him in two presidential elections.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: One-handed mechanic repairs up to five motorcycles a day
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Despite losing an arm in a 2019 motorcycle crash, a 32-year-old mechanic here can still repair up to five motorcycles a day using only one hand.
Samsul Aripin Sadip, from Kota Tinggi, said many people are amazed by his ability to fix motorcycles with one hand and often assume he was born that way.
He said the crash occurred in 2019 while he was test-riding a customer's motorcycle from Sungai Danga to Puteri Harbour, when the machine skidded and slammed into a road divider.
Severe injuries forced doctors at Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) here to amputate his arm to save his life.
"I was told that if I did not undergo the surgery, I faced risks that could affect my brain nerves.
"I believe in Allah's plan, and I accepted my fate at the time because I was thinking about my future and did not want to burden my parents.
"My parents were also my source of strength. Although they were initially distressed by what happened, I rested for a few months before retraining myself to repair motorcycles using my left hand.
"It was certainly a challenge because it felt awkward working with my left hand after being used to my right, but with continuous practice, my confidence grew," said Samsul Aripin, who now lives at Flat Sri Lanang in Tebrau.
He said he was grateful to receive job offers from several motorcycle workshops and has been working at a workshop in Jalan Harmonium 23/14, Taman Desa Tebrau here for the past year.
He is able to repair between two and five motorcycles daily, depending on whether the damage involves the engine or only external parts.
"I have had a passion for fixing motorcycles since I was 14, when I was in Form Two, and it allowed me to earn a side income as a teenager.
"No matter the damage, including on high-powered motorcycles, I try my best to fix it without giving up, and if it takes too long, I ask my colleagues for help.
"I work from noon to 11pm, and I am grateful that customers are satisfied with my work."
Samsul Aripin added that he hopes to deepen his skills in the field and inspire others facing similar adversity.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib pardon minutes set for declassification process
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The process of declassifying minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting concerning former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional pardon is being arranged, subject to legal requirements.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the process was under way.
"The cabinet is advised by the attorney-general on this matter.
"However, the intention is indeed there, and it will go through the prescribed, mandatory process," he told reporters at his weekly post-cabinet press conference.
Yesterday, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail told Parliament that he would propose at today's cabinet meeting that the minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting concerning Najib's conditional pardon be declassified.
The proposal followed a question from Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman on whether the government would seek to declassify the minutes to address allegations of non-compliance or government interference in the implementation of Najib's conditional pardon.
Saifuddin said the matter fell under the
jurisdiction
of the attorney-general.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar praises HKL surgeons' feat in reattaching cop's hand
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) surgeons for reattaching a policeman's severed hand following a parang attack in Kepong.
"I also want to congratulate the head of the surgical and rehabilitation team that has made us proud at HKL.
"So to all the staff at HKL, I congratulate you for being able to reattach the hand in a rather complex operation that requires extraordinary expertise, and I pray that the work and its results turn out well," he said after performing Friday prayers at Madrasathul Gouthiyyah Surau in Brickfields.
Lance Corporal Thierry Rodger Fendy, who is attached to the Gombak police headquarters,
suffered injuries to his right hand
during a confrontation with an armed foreigner at an apartment in Desa Amanpuri on Wednesday.
The policeman was rushed to
HKL for emergency treatment
following the attack, where the hospital's Upper Limb and Microsurgery subspecialty team, led by Dr Allan Ravi Rajagopal and Dr Aziz Sabbir Husain, performed the eight-hour procedure.
Anwar said he had told the cabinet meeting earlier that the government must support the security forces.
"So in the cabinet meeting just now, I said we must give firm support to our security machinery and forces.
"We cannot compromise with crime, and being firm should not be taken lightly," he said.
Following the successful surgery, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry remained committed to ensuring Thierry received comprehensive medical care to support his recovery and restore optimal hand function.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor told to speed up drain, river cleaning to reduce floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Selangor needs to speed up drain and river cleaning to reduce flooding, following Kuala Lumpur's example, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
"The menteri besar (Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari) has approved additional funding and action at all levels. But we feel there is a need to move faster, as Kuala Lumpur does.
"In Kuala Lumpur, drains and rivers are cleaned six times a year instead of twice, helping to reduce flooding," he said.
Anwar was speaking to reporters after performing Friday prayers at Madrasathul Gouthiyyah Surau in Brickfields.
He said the menteri besar had provided additional funds, while district and municipal councils had been instructed to ensure drains and waterways were cleaned.
"Starting today, there must be no delays. We are taking action to the best of our ability," he said.
As of 8am today, the number of flood victims at relief centres had increased in Selangor but decreased in Perak.
In Selangor, the number of flood victims at seven relief centres rose to 1,248 from 1,144, while the number of families increased to 338 from 318 yesterday.
Selangor has been hit by repeated flash floods in recent weeks, with Kampung Melayu Subang among the worst-affected areas.
Nearly
550 homes and about 1,500 residents
in the village were affected by four floods, with damage reported to homes, vehicles and belongings.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 64,100 litres of diesel worth RM1.07mil seized in Kedah raid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Authorities seized 64,100 litres of suspected misappropriated diesel worth RM439,085 and arrested four people, including a foreigner, during a raid at an industrial premises in Kedah on Wednesday.
The 11.30pm raid was carried out by Bukit Aman's Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence (WCB/PSK) under the Internal Security and Public Order Department, in collaboration with Kedah Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry enforcement officers.
WCB/PSK commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said those detained were believed to have acted as lorry drivers, workers and the premises owner.
He said further checks at the site led to the seizure of equipment and vehicles believed to have been used in the diesel misappropriation activity.
"The seizures involved two tanker lorries containing about 4,500 litres and 14,000 litres of diesel respectively, as well as three skid tanks containing about 18,000 litres, 13,000 litres and 14,000 litres of the fuel.
"Also seized were an intermediate bulk container (IBC) tank holding about 600 litres of diesel, two oil suction pumps, two metered suction pumps, three mobile phones, as well as equipment and vehicle keys believed to be linked to the activity," he said in a statement today.
Zaki said the total value of the seizures, including related components, was estimated at RM1,074,585.
All suspects, together with the seized vehicles, diesel and equipment, were handed over to the Kedah Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry and the Kuala Muda police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Department for further action and investigation.
"Investigations are also focusing on the involvement of each suspect and identifying whether there are other networks or parties linked to the misappropriation," he said.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 21 of the Control of Supplies Act 1961 and Section 55B of the Immigration Act 1959/63, adding that enforcement will be intensified through intelligence, monitoring and integrated operations to curb the misappropriation and abuse of controlled goods.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UEC holders remain eligible to take up medical degrees at private universities
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Unified Examination Certificate (UEC) holders who meet the minimum entry requirement of B4 in five stipulated subjects will remain eligible to apply for direct entry into medical degree programmes at private universities.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the cabinet had decided to retain the entry requirements that were in place before the recent amendment to the Education Act.
"Therefore, UEC holders who meet the minimum requirement of B4 in the five stipulated subjects remain eligible to apply for direct entry into medical degree programmes at private higher education institutions (IPTS)," he said at his weekly post-cabinet meeting press conference.
Under the amendment, the UEC, administered by the United Chinese School Committees' Association of Malaysia (Dong Zong) for Chinese independent secondary schools, is not recognised by the federal government as an entry qualification for public universities.
Fahmi said the Health Ministry and Malaysian Medical Council (MMC) would coordinate follow-up action with the Higher Education Ministry to ensure the admission process ran smoothly and address any issues that might arise.
He said the move would also ensure that the standards and quality of medical education in the country, including at private institutions, remained protected.
B4 is equivalent to a credit grade under the UEC grading system.
Under existing MMC guidelines, UEC qualifications are recognised for admission into medical programmes at private higher education institutions only.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Rafie vows inclusive development for Paya Rumput residents
Article:
MELAKA: Perikatan Nasional candidate for Paya Rumput Rafie Ahmad wants to continue the development initiatives undertaken by the previous assemblyman while addressing residents' concerns over flooding and traffic congestion in the constituency.
Rafie said the issues were among the main complaints raised by residents during the first three days of campaigning, with traffic congestion partly attributed to the large number of traffic lights in the area.
He said he also wanted to address the needs of residents as Paya Rumput continued to experience population growth.
"My hopes for Paya Rumput go beyond seeing taller buildings or wider roads. I want to see our children receive a good education, our young people have opportunities to build their future, mothers have avenues to earn an income, and every family enjoy a better quality of life," he said.
He said development should not be measured solely by physical infrastructure, but also by how much people's lives could be improved.
"Ultimately, development is not just about what we build, but whose lives we manage to improve.
"I do not want to make promises that I may not be able to fulfil. If entrusted with the responsibility, I will do my best to carry it out. I want to continue listening to the community, learning from shortcomings and working towards solutions," he said.
Rafie said he was ready to shoulder the responsibility and work with the people, regardless of their race, age or background, to make Paya Rumput a better place to live and raise future generations.
He said cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and PN under the Muafakat Melaka slogan had given their campaign machinery an advantage, with both sides working together to reach out to voters.
He said the approach was important as Paya Rumput had more than 46,000 voters from various ethnic backgrounds.
Of the total, more than 30,000 were Malay voters, while over 13,000 were Chinese and nearly 3,000 were Indian.
"We do not differentiate based on race, religion or background. Instead, we work fairly for all communities, be they Malay, Chinese or Indian," he said.
Rafie is facing a three-cornered contest in Paya Rumput against Pakatan Harapan candidate Datuk Azman Abidin and Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar of Parti Bersama Malaysia.
In the 2021 Melaka election, BN's Datuk Rais Yasin won the seat with 6,830 votes.
For this election, the seat was allocated to PN as part of the cooperation between BN and PN, while Rais is contesting in Sungai Udang.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Body of Indian national found, seventh victim of Sungai Pertak water surge, one still missing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The body of the seventh victim of the water surge incident at the Sungai Pertak Picnic Site near here was found at 3.40pm today, leaving only one of the eight people reported missing still unaccounted for.
According to the latest information from the Incident Command Post (PKTK), the body of the adult Indian national was found in Sector C of the search area.
The victim was pronounced dead by an assistant medical officer from the Rasa Health Clinic at 4.45pm after being brought to the PKTK.
The body was subsequently handed over to the police at 4.59pm before being taken to Sungai Buloh Hospital for a post-mortem.
Following the discovery, the search and rescue (SAR) operation, now in its fifth day, continued with the focus on Sectors C and D to locate the remaining missing victim.
Today’s SAR operation began at 7am, with additional personnel from the Special Tactical Operations and Rescue Team Malaysia of the Fire and Rescue Department.
Also deployed were the Selangor Special Incident and Emergency Response Rapid Team of the Malaysian Civil Defence Force and Forestry Department Mountain Guides, as well as two drone units from the Air Operations Force to assist in searching the water surface.
Yesterday, the body of the sixth victim, identified as a Yemeni national, was found floating at 10.15am at the river mouth near the Pertak Bridge.
In the incident at about 5.30pm last Monday, eight men, comprising one local and seven foreigners from Yemen, Sri Lanka, Nepal and India, were reported missing after being swept away by strong currents. — Bernama

Title: Najib spends nearly eight hours out of Taman Duta residence for Friday prayers, returns at 6.27pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak returned to his residence in Taman Duta at about 6.27pm today, concluding an outing that lasted nearly eight hours.
According to a report by
Sin Chew Daily
, Najib left his home at approximately 10.28am and was escorted directly by prison department vehicles.
The former leader was spotted leaving for Friday prayers this morning before making his way back to his residence in the evening.
Najib is currently serving the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest at his Jalan Langgak Duta residence until August 23, 2028, following a conditional royal pardon granted in September.
Under the strict conditions set by the Pardons Board, he is barred from engaging in political activities, making media statements, or appearing on social media.
He is also prohibited from leaving the gazetted premises without written permission, although prison officers are permitted to escort him for Friday prayers.

Title: Amirudin unveils ‘Kita Selangor’ special financial aid with two months’ salary for civil servants, minimum RM1,000
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 13 — The Selangor State Government today announced a Special Financial Assistance (BKK) equivalent to two months’ salary for civil servants in the state.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said this incentive serves as a token of appreciation for the hard work of civil servants in delivering aid to the people, particularly through the implementation of the Pakej Pengukuhan Daya Tahan Selangor.
He noted that the implementation of this package has helped empower vulnerable groups, school students, working women, farmers, and padi farmers as they navigate the global energy crisis.
“The state government is announcing the ‘Kita Selangor’ Special Financial Assistance (BKK) for the year 2026, amounting to two months’ salary or allowance, with a minimum payment of RM1,000.
“This payment will be drawn from current-year allocations and will cover the emoluments of state government personnel including those whose salaries are paid by the federal government as well as teachers of ‘Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain’ (KAFA) religious classes, with a total financial implication of RM100.31 million.
“God willing, the ‘Kita Selangor’ BKK will be disbursed by December 21,” he said while tabling the Selangor Budget 2027 today.
Meanwhile, Amirudin said the state government proposed an increase in the monthly allowance for KAFA teachers by RM200, raising the total allowance from RM1,500 to RM1,700 starting from January 2027.
He said the proposal would involve 7,245 KAFA teachers appointed by the state and the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (JAKIM), including 4,303 JAIS Fardhu Ain Teachers (GAF) and 2,942 JAKIM KAFA Teachers.
“The Selangor State Government always recognises the contributions and sacrifices of KAFA teachers as the main pillar in shaping a generation that is knowledgeable, faithful and of noble character. Therefore, the welfare and well-being of religious educators must continue to be prioritised, especially in facing the rising cost of living.
“This initiative is an initial step towards aligning the welfare of religious educators while appreciating their role in educating more than 100,000 students throughout Selangor. The increase in this allowance involves an additional financial implication of RM14 million, which will be covered by the state government,” he said.
He also said that the state government also plans to increase the allowance for KAFA teacher — those appointed by the state as well as by JAKIM — to RM2,000, in line with the new federal minimum wage rate that will take effect from June 2027. — Bernama

Title: Amirudin: Sungai Klang, Sungai Langat among river basins in Selangor’s RM36.45m flood mitigation plan
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 13 — The Selangor government has allocated RM36.45 million for 47 immediate flood mitigation projects under the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS) for 2027.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, when tabling the state’s Budget 2027, said that of the total, RM9.15 million would be for the Sungai Klang basin and RM7.35 million for the development of the Sungai Langat basin.
He said the allocation would also cover the Sungai Buloh, Sungai Selangor, Sungai Bernam and Sungai Kapar Besar river basins, as well as preparatory works such as design, surveying and land matters.
He added that, of the 47 projects, 30 are continuation projects, of which 13 have been completed and are undergoing final account preparation, nine are being implemented, two are at the pre-tender stage while six are at the design stage.
“As for the 17 new projects, one is at the design stage, 11 are in the process of appointing consultants and five are still at the planning stage,” he said at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly sitting today.
Amirudin also said that RM19.38 million had been allocated for 25 irrigation system projects, RM17.90 million for 16 river basin development and management projects, and RM6.63 million for nine environmentally friendly irrigation projects.
For flood mitigation projects under the Selangor Maritime Gateway Economic Development Zone (SMG ZPE), RM25 million has been proposed to continue works to increase river capacity and improve water flow, with the projects having achieved 71.43 per cent physical progress.
While physical works are underway, Amirudin said the disaster warning system between the state and district operation centres and agencies on the ground would also be improved.
“Through the Community-Based Disaster Risk Management Programme and training in schools, we want residents to know where they need to go, who to contact and how to assist those who need support to evacuate,” he added.
Amirudin also wants the Public Works Department (JKR), local authorities (PBTs) and the JPS to prioritise projects that resolves flooding problems, including culverts and drainage systems.
“Technical reviews that can be conducted concurrently should be initiated simultaneously. If a decision involves multiple agencies, the matter must be brought to the relevant authorities who can resolve it at an earlier stage.
“The Netherlands’ experience offers us a guide on what needs to be accelerated and one of the initiatives is the integration of embankments and water control structures with planning that allows rivers to overflow more safely,” he added.
Meanwhile, he said the state government would provide a public dashboard displaying project locations, implementing agencies and updates on implementation phases, from the appointment of design consultants and contractors to the progress of on-site works.
“Before the monsoon season begins, the government will update the status of flood-prone locations, detailing the related projects, appointments that have been made and works expected to be completed in time.
“With this information, residents can know the level of protection in their areas ahead of the rainy season and refer directly to the agencies responsible,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MB: Selangor budgets RM559m for 6,000km of ageing pipes, RM3.5m for water master plan
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 13 — The Selangor government has allocated RM559 million next year to replace ageing pipes in the state to ensure a more stable water supply for consumers.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said more than 6,000 kilometres (km) of ageing pipes needed replacing, and the state government has increased its annual allocation starting from 2024 to expedite the effort.
“The pipe replacement programme was first implemented in 2016, with an annual target of replacing 150km of pipes.
“However, starting from 2024, the state government and Air Selangor Sdn Bhd (Air Selangor) have increased the replacement rate to 300km annually,” he said when tabling the Selangor 2027 Budget here today.
He said a total of 1,231.01km of ageing pipes had been replaced as of August this year.
Meanwhile, Amirudin said the state government had also allocated RM120.8 million for the Non-Revenue Water (NRW) Reduction Programme, which includes the installation of Pressure Transient and Permanent Leak Noise Correlating Loggers (PLNCL) and Advanced Pressure Management Systems (APMS).
“The NRW rate is targeted to be reduced to 26.3 per cent this year and 25.8 per cent in 2027, compared with 26.8 per cent in 2025.
“The annual reduction of 0.5 percentage points is in line with the target set by Air Selangor and submitted to the National Water Services Commission (SPAN),” he said.
Amirudin said the state government had also allocated RM101 million to further ensure a clean water supply, including through the Raw Water Guarantee Scheme, which aims to protect water treatment plant operations from disruptions caused by pollution.
In addition, he said RM3.5 million had been allocated for a study on the Selangor Water Master Plan 2025-2050 as part of long-term planning. The master plan will coordinate the management of raw water, treated water and wastewater with flood management and is expected to be completed in 2028. — Bernama

Title: Selangor allocates RM24m to boost public transport use to 60pc, says MB
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 13 — The Selangor state government has allocated RM24 million for the public transport sector in 2027, aiming to increase public transport usage among state residents to 60 per cent from the current 40 per cent.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the allocation would support efforts to develop a more people-friendly public transport ecosystem, including improving bus services, providing fare subsidies and expanding pedestrian routes.
He said that although public transport officially came under the jurisdiction of the federal government, Selangor, with a population of nearly 7.5 million, needed to take proactive steps to complement federal-level efforts.
“To develop a well-structured first- and last-mile connectivity system that complements a comprehensive public transport ecosystem in Selangor, the state government has allocated RM24 million for the sector in 2027,” he said when tabling the Selangor Budget 2027 at the Selangor State Legislative Assembly here today.
Amirudin said RM12 million had been allocated to improve the efficiency and optimise the routes of the Smart Selangor Bus service, which would be rebranded as Bas Kita Selangor.
He said the improvements would include more systematic route management and increased service frequency to connect residents to rail stations and key areas in the state.
He said the state government would also introduce the SEL 30 Programme in 2027, with an allocation of RM5 million to provide a RM30 monthly public transport subsidy, expected to benefit 13,000 users.
The programme aims to reduce travel costs for Selangor residents while encouraging more people to use bus and rail services.
To improve access to public transport, Amirudin said the state government, through local authorities, would build 35 kilometres of new pedestrian walkways across Selangor to facilitate access to key destinations, including public transport stations.
He said the Pedestrian Audit would also be completed by the end of this year and used as a reference to address issues concerning pedestrian facilities and walkway safety.
In addition, the state government would introduce Selangor Mobility Nexus, an integrated mobility data and information centre to make public transport information more accessible through a single system.
Amirudin said the initiative aimed to reduce duplication among existing applications and systems, enabling users to check bus stop locations, arrival times and route information more easily.
He said the development of Selangor Mobility Nexus would be supported by Rantaian Mesra Sdn Bhd at a cost of RM1.5 million, focusing on data integration, including journey planning, Scan-to-Ride, complaint management and mobility route mapping. — Bernama

Title: Federal Court sets Feb 25 to hear Altantuya family’s leave to appeal over reduced RM1.4m award
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 13 — The Federal Court has fixed February 25 next year to hear an application by the family of murdered Mongolian national Altantuya Shaariibuu for leave to appeal against a Court of Appeal ruling that reduced the damages awarded over her death in 2006.
Lawyer Abraham Au, representing political analyst Abdul Razak Baginda, confirmed the date when contacted by Bernama.
He said the court also set Dec 3 to hear the family’s application to amend its notice of motion seeking leave to appeal, following case management before Federal Court deputy registrar Rohaiza Hamzah yesterday.
Altantuya’s family filed the leave application on February 19 this year after the Court of Appeal reduced the damages awarded to them from RM5 million to RM1.4 million.
On January 20, the appellate court also ruled that the government was not vicariously liable for the actions of former police officers Sirul Azhar Umar and Azilah Hadri.
The family filed a RM100 million civil suit against Abdul Razak, Azilah, Sirul Azhar and the government in 2007, claiming that Altantuya’s death had caused them mental shock and psychological trauma.
In 2022, the Shah Alam High Court ordered the defendants to pay RM5 million in damages to the family.
Azilah and Sirul Azhar were convicted of Altantuya’s murder in 2009. The Court of Appeal subsequently acquitted them, but the Federal Court overturned the acquittals and reinstated their convictions in 2015.
In 2023, the Federal Court commuted Azilah’s death sentence to 40 years’ imprisonment after allowing his review application under the Revision of Sentence of Death and Imprisonment for Natural Life (Temporary Jurisdiction of the Federal Court) Act 2023. — Bernama

Title: It’s final: Dutch model Ivana Smit’s mother stops pursuing lawsuit against govt over probe of 2017 death
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 13 — The late Dutch model Ivana Smit’s family has decided to not continue pursuing a lawsuit against the Malaysian government at the Federal Court over alleged negligence in a probe of her 2017 death, the family’s lawyer Datuk Sankara Nair confirmed today.
This brings Smit’s family’s six-year legal bid in court to an end, but Sankara said the authorities should continue to investigate her death and to regularly communicate with her family.
“Ivana’s family has decided not to seek leave to appeal to the Federal Court against the Court of Appeal’s decision of October 14, 2026. Accordingly, these civil proceedings have come to an end.
“Their decision deserves respect and should not be understood as satisfaction with the investigation or acceptance that their concerns have been answered,” he said in a statement today.
Tomorrow would be the last day to file for leave to appeal the Court of Appeal’s October 14 decision, and not filing for it would mean the family is not pursuing the lawsuit.
The Court of Appeal decision was not in Smit’s family’s favour.
But Sankara today also commended the Court of Appeal for its “firm, emphatic and stern” verbal remarks when delivering its decision on October 14, where it cautioned that this does not exonerate past shortcomings and emphasised the police’s continuing responsibility to pursue viable leads diligently and keep the family regularly informed.
He made it clear that the court had made these observations orally, and that this was not part of a formal or written order that directed the police to give updates to Smit’s family.
“The conclusion of this civil action leaves the authorities’ investigative responsibilities intact. We call upon them to heed the Court’s oral observations through sustained investigative effort and clear, regular communication with Ivana’s family.
“The family has chosen to bring its civil litigation to a close. The authorities must continue their work towards establishing the truth surrounding Ivana’s death,” he concluded in the statement.
Tomorrow would be the last day to file for leave to appeal the Court of Appeal’s October 14 decision, and not filing for it would mean the family is not pursuing the lawsuit. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
What happened before this
On December 7, 2017, 18-year-old Smit was found nude and dead on the sixth floor of CapSquare Residence, a condominium off Jalan Dang Wangi in Kuala Lumpur, after having fallen from a unit on the 20th floor.
The Coroner’s Court on March 18, 2019 in an inquest found that Smit’s death was caused by a “misadventure”.
But the High Court on November 22, 2019 replaced the inquest findings by saying that Smit’s death was caused by “a person or persons unknown”, and ordered the police to start investigations again.
In November 2020, Smit’s mother Christina Carolina Gerarda Johanna Verstappen filed a civil suit against the inspector-general of police, Dang Wangi investigating officer ASP Faizal Abdullah, the home minister, and the Malaysian government over alleged breach of duties and negligence in investigating the cause of her daughter’s 2017 death.
On July 29, 2025, the High Court ordered all those sued to pay RM1.1 million compensation, and declared the police as having failed to carry out their duties to restart investigations as ordered in 2019.
Also on July 29, 2025, the High Court issued a court order known as a “mandamus order”, which included ordering the police to restart investigations on Smit’s death and to brief the Attorney General’s Chambers every three months with updates on the investigation.
On October 14, 2026, the Court of Appeal set aside the High Court’s decision, including the RM1.1 million award.
Among other things, the Court of Appeal reportedly ruled that the police’s public duty to investigate crime does not give rise to a private duty of care that would result in compensation to individual victims or their relatives for perceived investigation failures.
The Court of Appeal had also ruled that the decisions from the inquest and the 2019 criminal revision at the High Court could not by themselves establish civil liability in a separate case, Sankara said today.
In his statement today, Sankara also said the Court of Appeal’s October 14 decision does not mean that public authorities would have blanket immunity, but said it is a “substantial obstacle” for families who are pursuing such court claims over alleged negligence in investigations of deaths.
“We respectfully recognise the courts’ responsibility to apply established legal principles. Nevertheless, concerns about exposing public authorities to excessive litigation must be weighed against the need for meaningful accountability.
“A public duty must carry practical substance for the people it exists to protect. Where the law restricts civil redress, the case for effective independent oversight and legislative consideration becomes all the more pressing and compelling,” he said in the same statement.
